title: Quant kernel impact playbook - quant tradeoff matrix and microbench notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic playbook for evaluating per-kernel behavior under different quantization schemes (INT8, FP8, GPTQ-style per-layer calibration, and AWQ). The goal is to produce a compact tradeoff matrix that teams can use to pick a kernel+quant combo for a target latency/cost/quality point and to surface common bottlenecks that appear only under certain kernels or model shapes.

Scope and motivation:
- Focus: medium-to-large causal transformer decoders we run in production (seq lengths 8..1024, batch sizes 1..16 typical).
- Why: we've seen contradictory signals between microbenchmarks (single-op flops) and end-to-end latency. Some kernels win in throughput but regress tail latency; quantization sometimes amplifies attention scatter or cache pressure.
- Deliverable: a small checklist, an experiment matrix, representative microbench outputs and interpretive notes. Not exhaustive; this is a working explainer for eng teams onboarding new quant kernels.

Quick recommendations (high level):
- If 99th percentile latency and low jitter are the priority: default to the "conservative" kernel profile (int8 with per-layer calibration + activation clipping) on GPUs with larger L2. Avoid AWQ packing until you can confirm KV cache pressure.
- If cost/throughput dominates and tail is acceptable: AWQ + specialized continuous-batching kernels give the best token cost for batch >= 4 for seq <= 256.
- FP8 shows minimal quality delta on most tasks vs FP16 in our tests, but only with kernels that support robust exp/normalize numerics. Some FP8 kernels caused rare NaN bursts during long-stream decoding.

Experiment matrix (canonical):
- Models: smallgpt-6B (6B dense decoder), medium-12B (12B mixture, 1M params test shape), longform-30B (attention-heavy).
- Quant schemes: int8-symmetric, int8-asymmetric, awq-4bit (per-channel), gptq-8bit calibrate (layerwise), fp8-e4m3.
- Kernels: baseline-fp16 (cuBLAS-like), kernelA-int8-packed, kernelB-int8-unpacked, kernelC-awq-packed, kernelD-fp8-stable, kernelE-mixed-precision-fallback.
- Workloads: interactive single-turn (batch=1, seq=64), chat-turn (batch=4, seq=128), long-generate (batch=2, seq=1024 dynamic).

Microbench results (summaries, numbers are median of 10 runs unless noted). Full logs attached in linked artifacts.
1) smallgpt-6B, interactive (batch=1, seq=64):
  - baseline-fp16: p50=42ms, p95=58ms, tokens/s=240, perplexity delta vs FP16=0.0
  - kernelA-int8-packed: p50=28ms, p95=65ms, tokens/s=360, perplexity delta=+0.6
  - kernelB-int8-unpacked: p50=33ms, p95=48ms, tokens/s=310, perplexity delta=+0.3
  - kernelC-awq-packed: p50=25ms, p95=90ms (noticeable tail), tokens/s=400, perplexity delta=+1.2
  Notes: AWQ-packed gave best median but worst tail. Profile shows sporadic GPU kernel launches with >5ms gaps (likely synchronized memcpy/packing).

2) medium-12B, chat-turn (batch=4, seq=128):
  - baseline-fp16: p50=120ms, p95=165ms, tokens/s=210
  - kernelA-int8-packed: p50=85ms, p95=150ms, tokens/s=320
  - kernelD-fp8-stable: p50=95ms, p95=110ms, tokens/s=280, quality delta~+0.1
  - kernelE-mixed-precision-fallback: p50=105ms, p95=145ms, tokens/s=260, observed intermittent fallback to FP16 for attention-block 5 on long sequences.
  Notes: FP8 kernelD gave smoother tails; mixed-precision fallback has stability but cost variability due to occasional FP16 slow path.

3) longform-30B, long-generate (batch=2, seq=1024):
  - baseline-fp16: p50=980ms, p95=1,150ms, tokens/s=60
  - kernelB-int8-unpacked: p50=720ms, p95=900ms, tokens/s=82, quality delta=+0.8
  - kernelC-awq-packed: p50=640ms, p95=1,300ms, tokens/s=92, quality delta=+2.4 (fewer hallucinations on some prompts but worse in others)
  Observations: large seq -> AWQ unpack/pack and KV cache miss patterns amplify tail. Trace shows repeated device-host-control syncs originating in packing layer around attention KV write.

Bottleneck profiling notes (how we traced tails):
- Use mixed sampling: lightweight NVTX spans around each major op, and occasional nsight systems traces for the worst runs. The patterns to watch for:
  1) Interleaved memcpy+kernel micro stalls: look for small memcpy blocks in between kernels; this often means packing/format conversion on CPU.
  2) Kernel launch serialization: some custom packed kernels do serialized work queues with per-row mutexes under heavy batch concurrency.
  3) KV cache eviction/fragmentation: AWQ's packed layout increases memory fragmentation on long sequences causing GC-like page faults in CUDA Unified Memory setups.

Quality measurement guidelines (do not just use perplexity):
- Use a small eval set with structural checks (e.g., named-entity consistency), next-token accuracy on curated prompts, and long-range coherence tests.
- Compute both static deltas (perplexity or logprob) and black-box quality metrics (ROUGE/EM for retrieval tasks, hallucination flags for QA).
- Keep a small suite of adversarial prompts (we maintain 120 prompts) that historically surface regressions for INT8 and AWQ.

Checklist for kernel onboarding (practical steps):
1) Run microbench p50/p95 for three representative models (small/medium/large) and three seq shapes.
2) Capture NVTX spans across 20 runs; flag any run where p95/p50 > 2x for deeper tracing.
3) Run quality eval suite (120 prompts) and compute delta distributions.
4) Inspect GPU memory growth across long-run session (>= 1k tokens) for gradual leaks or fragmentation.
5) If AWQ or packed kernels show tail spikes, toggle packing granularity and remeasure; sometimes switching per-channel packing to per-block reduces memcpy overhead.

Common surprises and mitigations observed in practice:
- Surprise: Packed AWQ gives excellent median but tails balloon due to CPU packing. Mitigation: move packing to a pinned-memory prefetch worker that feeds a single-stream CUDA queue, reducing launch jitter.
- Surprise: Some FP8 kernels rely on unstable exp approximations that degrade on long-tail token distributions. Mitigation: set a fallback to FP16 for numerics-sensitive layers (softmax/ln) or add shared scaling across attention blocks.
- Surprise: Mixed-precision fallback increases variance in latency because fallback occurs intermittently only for some batches. Mitigation: perform a cheap pre-check pass (max activation estimate) and mark sequence as "will require FP16" to avoid mid-run mode switches.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Quantization-aware KV-cache layout: can we design an AWQ layout that avoids per-step packing overhead by keeping KV in a near-native GPU layout? (Spike: prototype in branch "kv-awq-layout-v2").
- Consistency of FP8 across GPU generations: run the same FP8 kernel across A100/RTXA6000/4090 and collect numerics anomalies.
- Fine-grained tail mitigation: evaluate colocated async memcpy + persistent CUDA stream feeding vs single-stream serialized launches.

Appendix: sample microbench command lines (for reproducibility)
- run_single.py --model smallgpt-6B --kernel kernelA --quant int8 --batch 1 --seq 64 --runs 10 --nvtx
- run_batch.py --model longform-30B --kernel kernelC --quant awq --batch 2 --seq 1024 --profile nsight

Notes to reviewers:
- Logs for the above runs are in linked_artifacts (see PR 2431). Please pay attention to the sample p95 outliers and the NVTX span ordering; both point to packing+sync behavior.
- This doc is intended to be a short, actionable guide for teams evaluating new quant kernels. Expect to iterate as new kernel versions land.
